paper_id: Zhang et al. - 2020 - airFinger Micro Finger Gesture Recognition via NIR Light Sensing for Smart Devices
title: airFinger: Micro Finger Gesture Recognition via NIR Light Sensing for Smart Devices
motivation: Small wearables need unobtrusive input; existing sensing modalities (radar/RF/camera) consume too much energy or have privacy/environment vulnerabilities
problem_framing: NIR sensing can't track finger movements—only detect gestures—which limits application scope for micro finger interactions
key_insight: RSS patterns from reflected NIR are unique per gesture AND per movement; feature importance feedback selects 25 robust features to handle individual/inconsistency variation
method_signature: Custom NIR LED-PD sensor with SBC noise mitigation + Dynamic Threshold segmentation + RF classifier + ZEBRA tracking algorithm
evaluation_criteria: Gesture recognition accuracy (98.72%) over 10,000 samples from 10 volunteers; robustness to individual diversity, inconsistency, environment
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Sunlight saturation outdoors causes PD saturation; direct IR remote pointing causes recognition errors
evidence_for_taste: how to precisely track fingers from RSS patterns is an issue that has not been studied
Ndyn has a lower magnitude comparing to Sges
RF has lower computational expense, which is more suitable for real-time
velocity is proportional to the time difference delta t
thinking_moves: 从信号幅值建模转向相对顺序建模
用特征重要性反馈指导特征选择，而非预设特征
将tracking问题分解为方向/速度/位移三个独立子问题
动态阈值替代固定阈值以适应个体差异
借鉴计算机视觉背景前景分割思想解决分割问题
